blocks.h2: What Does an Ejector Pump Do?
blocks.body: An ejector pump lives in a sealed basin in the basement floor. Basement fixtures that sit below the sewer line, like a toilet, shower, laundry or bar sink, drain into it. When the basin fills, the pump pushes the wastewater up and out to the sewer line or septic system. If your home has an [overhead sewer system](/mchenry/overhead-sewer-systems), every basement drain relies on it.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.intro: Stop using basement fixtures and call if:

tiles.h3: The Alarm Panel Is Lit Up
tiles.body: A rising basin. Stop using the basement toilet, shower and washer.

tiles.h3: Sewage Smell in the Lower Level
tiles.body: A lid seal or vent connection has failed.

tiles.h3: The Pump Hums but Nothing Moves
tiles.body: A jammed impeller, often from wipes.
On and off every few seconds points to a float or check valve problem.

blocks.intro: Many McHenry homes with a basement bathroom rely on an ejector pump.

items.body: About 4 in 10 McHenry homes went up in those years, and a basement bathroom in one of them likely has its original pump. Their original ejector pumps are now past their expected life.

items.h3: Pumps That Feed a Septic Tank
items.body: Outside city sewer in McHenry County, ejector pumps often lift wastewater to a septic system. We service those setups and can tell you when the problem is the tank, not the pump.
Homes that converted to an [overhead sewer system](/mchenry/overhead-sewer-systems) after high water depend on the ejector for every basement drain.
Mineral buildup can make float switches stick. We check them during every service.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Can I keep using the upstairs bathrooms if the ejector fails?
items.preview: Usually, yes. Only basement fixtures drain to the pump.
items.answer: Usually. Upstairs fixtures normally drain by gravity. Stop using everything in the basement until the pump is fixed. If your home has an overhead sewer, ask us when you call.

items.q: Is it the ejector pump or the septic tank?
items.preview: We check both. A full tank and a failed pump look similar.
items.answer: A full septic tank and a failed ejector pump can both cause basement backups. We check the pump, float and check valve and tell you if the tank needs pumping.

items.q: Why does my ejector pump keep jamming?
items.answer: Wipes, paper towels and hygiene products wrap around the impeller. Only toilet paper should go down a toilet that drains to an ejector.

items.q: How long does an ejector pump last?
items.answer: Many last somewhere between 7 and 10 years or more, less with heavy use or wipes.

items.q: What does ejector pump replacement cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. The price comes first.
items.answer: Every job is priced on the pump, basin, check valve, venting and access. You'll have a flat-rate number before we open the basin.
